blocks.x: Blockchain & Digital Trust — provenance, tokenization and credentials, argued from regulated deployments.

The chain is rarely the hard part. Instruments, transfer restrictions, custody, provenance law and credential usability decide whether digital-trust programs land — which is why our theses lead with legal and operational reality, not consensus mechanics.
Each position below has run under regulatory scrutiny; the engagement notes behind them are linked from every article.

items: Tokenization is a legal program with a cryptographic runtime
Instruments, transfer restrictions and custody decide success: not chain choice.
EUDR made provenance a compliance deadline
Chain-of-custody evidence is becoming a market-access requirement, not a marketing story.

blocks.x: Bring the provenance or tokenization question your auditors keep asking — leave with the architecture that answers it.
